reason: Phagocytes are shown clearing debris near the cut, a useful early part of wound repair.
expectation: The phagocytes will clear debris from the wound.

effect: The wound is now cleared of debris, so I can work on its blood supply and repair.
reaction: The result matched the pictured role of the phagocytes.
reason: The repair signals point toward the nearby vessel, suggesting they stimulate a blood supply for the wound.
expectation: The capillary will grow toward the wound.

effect: The repair signals produced a capillary sprout connected to the circulation, suggesting a growing supply for the wound.
reaction: The result matched the picture and made the vessel's role clearer.
reason: The new capillary branch appears intended to supply the cleaned wound.
expectation: The sprout will become part of the wound's blood supply.

effect: The wound now has connected capillary branches and needs a surface and supporting layer.
reaction: The named slots make the remaining repair work clearer.
reason: Fibroblasts and matrix nutrients appear to be the materials for rebuilding the wound's support.
expectation: The fibroblasts will use the nutrients to make supporting matrix.

effect: Fibroblasts used the supplied materials to make connective tissue, which appears to fill the support slot.
reaction: The collagen fibres make the tissue's supporting role clear.
reason: The new connective tissue belongs in the wound's supporting dermis.
expectation: The connective tissue will fill the support slot.

effect: The connective tissue fills the support slot; the wound still needs a surface.
reaction: The note that young tissue is weaker adds useful context.
reason: The epidermal edge cells need nutrients to rebuild the wound's surface.
expectation: The cells will produce a new surface layer.

effect: The edge cells produced a new epidermal surface that appears ready to fill the remaining slot.
reaction: The sheet extending across the gap makes the repair easy to picture.
reason: The new surface should close the wound over its connective-tissue support.
expectation: The new surface will fill the surface slot and close the wound.

effect: The new surface closed the wound, completing the first goal; the temporary clot still needs clearing.
reaction: The reminder that deeper tissue is still gaining strength adds useful context.
reason: Clot-clearing enzymes are shown breaking down fibrin, which held the platelet plug together.
expectation: The enzymes will clear the temporary fibrin clot from the healing wound.

effect: The enzymes cleared most of the temporary fibrin, completing the clot-clearing goal; the new tissue and maturing scar remain.
reaction: The distinction between clearing the clot and continuing to strengthen the repair was useful.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding the new surface was most worthwhile because the sheet of cells crossing the gap made wound closure easy to picture, while the result distinguished closure from deeper strengthening.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the capillary sprout to the body felt somewhat repetitive after the sprout was already described as connected to the circulation, though it established the repair slots.

surprise.text: I appreciated learning that the wound can be closed while its deeper tissue is still gaining strength.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary; the item pictures and wound-repair goals gave each combination a clear purpose.

continue.text: I would be interested in another chapter if it developed an overlapping body process with similarly clear cause and effect. This chapter's repair sequence was understandable, although several combinations were predictable.
